text:
mari: Quick FYI — after landing the int4 build for cormorant-v2-lite in canary, structured funcall parse failures jumped from ~0.4% to ~2.2% on the sample suite. Noticing most failures are small JSON objects (<= 150 tokens).

devin: ugh. do we have a small failing example? can we diff outputs fp16 vs int4?

mari: pasted one below (int4 output -> parser choke). full sample set uploaded to /runs/cormorant-v2-lite/canary/2026-03-22.zip but here's the minimal one: 

sam: ```
int4 output (trimmed):
{"action":"update_user","args":{"id":123,"attrs":{"name":"J\u2019on","email":"jon@example.com"}}}

parser error: Unexpected token \"\u2019\" in string (position 25)

fp16 output:
{"action":"update_user","args":{"id":123,"attrs":{"name":"J'on","email":"jon@example.com"}}}
```

anya: interesting — looks like a unicode normalization / tokenizer boundary causing smart quotes in int4. Could be quantization perturbing subtoken selection.

devin: metrics snapshot from canary-bot: 
canary-bot: Alert: funcall_parse_fail_rate increased to 2.2% (baseline 0.4%) for cormorant-v2-lite int4 on structured-output suite. 95th-latency unchanged.

mari: yes canary-bot flagged it at 03:12. Failures mostly on short name fields, emails OK. Pattern: apostrophe and non-ascii accented chars -> smart-quote or escaped sequences inserted.

sam: quick checks I ran: 
- re-run with kvcache disabled -> failure rate 2.1% (no change)
- lower temperature to 0.0 -> 1.9%
- switch to fp16 model -> 0.45%

anya: so quantization noise is the likely culprit. Two-prong plan: 1) try postprocess normalization (NFKC + replace smart quotes) as a stopgap in the structured-output layer; 2) run an int4 rerun with alternative tokenization bias (favor ascii tokens) and collect diffs.

mari: agreed. For (1) I can prototype a lightweight sanitizer in the parser that runs before strict JSON parsing: convert curly quotes to straight, normalize unicode, and reject if non-printing control chars present. That should heal most customer-visible failures quickly.

devin: please add a metric for how many messages repaired by sanitizer vs actual parse fails. We want to avoid masking real model regressions.

sam: for (2) I'll recompile the int4 kernel with smoother logits floor and force-lower-unkprob; launching a canary job now: job id runcanary-171800-2. ETA ~18m.

anya: also vote to add a small eval that specifically probes single-token punctuation boundaries e.g. names with apostrophes, accented chars, and emojis. Add to onboarding golden set.

mari: action items: 
- mari: implement sanitizer + metric hook (PR in 1h)
- sam: rerun int4 with alternative bias (job runcanary-171800-2)
- devin: add targeted testcases to onboarding suite and update canary gating thresholds

devin: I'll own gating change but let's keep it permissive until we confirm sanitizer doesn't hide major regressions.

sam: runcanary-171800-2 started. attaching quick diff when done.

mari: PR #4217 created: parser: add compact-json-whitelist-sentry sanitizer. Demo logs attached in PR.

anya: thanks all. if sanitizer reduces >80% of current parse failures we can ship it behind a feature flag to Dedicated and Hosted as a belt-and-braces fix. Long term we should fix quantization training / tokenizer pairing.

mari: note — disable sanitizer in 24h to ensure we don't blind regression detection; we'll flip it on for Hosted with telemetry.

canary-bot: Update: runcanary-171800-2 completed. int4 parse_fail_rate -> 1.05% (pre-sanitizer).

sam: will post full diff in ~10m. looks promising but not fully resolved.

mari: thanks — I'll follow up with PR review and a quick demo tomorrow morning.

anya: ping me when diff posted, will add cases to goldens. :thumbsup:
